cards.title: A repository
cards.body: A repository (repo) is a project folder that Git keeps track of. `git init` turns the folder you are in into one.
cards.code:
mkdir site
cd site
git init

hi.title: Repository
hi.body: Repository (repo) ek project folder hai jise Git track karta hai. `git init` aap jis folder mein ho use repo bana deta hai.

cards.title: Looking around
cards.body: `ls` lists what is in the folder you are in, `pwd` shows where you are, and `cd` moves into a folder (`cd ..` goes back out).
cards.code:
mkdir demo
cd demo
pwd
touch index.html
ls

hi.title: Aas paas dekhna
hi.body: `ls` batata hai folder mein kya hai, `pwd` dikhata hai aap kahan ho, aur `cd` kisi folder ke andar le jaata hai (`cd ..` wapas bahar).

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: One command here is not a Git command at all. Tap it.
cards.code:
mkdir notes
cd notes
git int

bug.fix: There is no `git int`. To start a repository, type `git init`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Yahan ek command Git command hai hi nahi. Us par tap karo.
hi.fix: `git int` jaisa kuch nahi hota. Repository shuru karne ke liye `git init` type karo.

check.question: Which command turns the current folder into a Git repository?
check.explanation: `git init` creates the hidden `.git` folder where Git keeps its history.

hi.question: Kaunsi command current folder ko Git repository banati hai?
hi.explanation: `git init` chhupa hua `.git` folder banata hai jahan Git apni history rakhta hai.

exercise.prompt: Your website's files are in the folder `site`. Go into it with `cd`, then turn it into a Git repository.
exercise.promptHi: Aapki website ki files `site` folder mein hain. `cd` se uske andar jao, phir use Git repository banao.
